reply_text:
I'd call this one **borderline**. The quote is on the page word for word, the date and role are fine, but it's unclear whether it counts as a claim about AI (part 2), and the rule says borderline cases stay out.

**1. Page check.** The page opened. It is OpenAI's own post, "Elon Musk wanted an OpenAI for-profit", which reprints the emails in full. Sutskever's email headed "Date: Fri, Feb 19, 2016, at 10:28 AM", to Elon Musk with Greg Brockman and Sam Altman copied, includes this bullet:

> "We will be able to achieve a conventionally significant result in the next 6 to 9 months, simply because the people we already have are very good. Achieving a field-altering result will be harder, riskier, and take longer. But we have a not unreasonable plan for that as well."

The quoted words match exactly; the search run just left off the last sentence. This is not a news report: it is the full text of his own email, published by the company. So it counts as his own words and the "coverage only" label doesn't apply.

**2. The admission rule, part by part.**
- **Part 1 (speaker and role): passes.** Sutskever is on the list. In February 2016 he was co-founder and chief scientist of OpenAI, per the role history I was given. The email is about the company's research plan, so he was writing as its chief scientist.
- **Part 2 (looks forward and is about AI): borderline.** The sentence does look forward. But it predicts what OpenAI's researchers will produce ("a conventionally significant result"), not something AI will do, reach or ship. "Conventionally significant" doesn't name any ability or product. It sits closer to a forecast about the company's own output than to a claim about AI. It isn't clearly a business forecast either, so I can't put it firmly on either side. The rule says such a case stays out and is logged as borderline.
- **Part 3 (a date or length of time): passes.** "The next 6 to 9 months" from 2016-02-19. Under the rule a range takes the later end, which is about November 2016. The "field-altering result" half has no date ("take longer"), so it could never be a claim on its own.
- **Part 4 (primary source): passes.** His own email, printed in full by OpenAI.
- **Already recorded?** No. None of his five recorded claim files is from 2016 or about this.

If the reviewer reads part 2 more loosely and lets it in, the bar would still have no outside test. The only test is "conventionally significant", which nobody outside could check, so it would probably be entered as unfalsifiable.
